summary: Gudrun Melzer is a scholar of Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctorate at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich under Jens-Uwe Hartmann and held a post at the University of Vienna.

Guo Jun is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Monash University, the University of Sydney, and Fuyan Buddhist Institute, and under Sheng Yen, Song Nian, and Qinyin. Around 2005, he served as abbot of Mahabodhi Monastery.
Guohui Shi is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Rissho University under Kenyu Mitomo and studied under Sheng Yen and several other teachers including Hoyo Watanabe and Toshinori Ochiai.

Gurinder Singh Mann is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He studied at the English and Foreign Languages University and Harvard University, and held posts at Columbia University (circa 1988–1999) and the University of California, Santa Barbara (circa 1999).

Gustaaf Houtman is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under Richard Burghart, also studying under Hla Pe and John Okell, and served there as a Senior Teaching Fellow.

Gustav Bickell was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and religious studies who studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg. He held academic posts at the University of Innsbruck (circa 1874–1891) and the University of Vienna (circa 1891–1906).

Gustav Haloun was a Sinologist who studied under August Conrady. He held positions at Charles University (circa 1927–1931), served as director at the University of Göttingen (circa 1931–1938), and was Professor of Chinese at the University of Cambridge (circa 1938–1951).

Gustav Roth was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Munich and studied at Patna University. He worked at the University of Göttingen (1959–1981) and served as Director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (1982–1985).

Guy Claxton is a scholar in education and Buddhist studies who founded the Sharpham College for Contemporary Buddhist Inquiry and served as Professor of the Learning Sciences at the University of Bristol from circa 1995 to 2008.

Guy G. Stroumsa is a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Harvard University, later serving at Hebrew University (circa 1978–2009) and the University of Oxford (circa 2009–2013).

Guy Newland is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, studied under Donald S. Lopez Jr. and the 14th Dalai Lama, and joined Central Michigan University around 1988.
Gyatsho Tshering was a Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Calcutta. He co-founded the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and served as its director from circa 1972 to 1995.

Gyoei Fukuda was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tendai Sect University. He held positions at the University of Tokyo in 1928, Toyo University from 1930 to 1931, and served as president of Taisho University from 1928 to 1934.
Gyoko Iotani is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University and later served there as an assistant professor.
Gyosho Takahashi is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a professor at both Minobusan Junior College and Minobusan University.
Gyoshu Chujo is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a professor at Minobusan Junior College and as a professor in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies at Minobusan University.
Gyu Eon Jang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a professorship at Peking University until 2011 and served as an HK research professor at Geumgang University.

Gyurme Dorje was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Edinburgh and earned a PhD at SOAS under Philip Denwood, followed by a fellowship at SOAS from circa 1987 to 1996.

György Hazai was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies who studied at Eötvös Loránd University (circa 1949–1954) and held a post at the German Academy of Sciences at Berlin (circa 1963–1983).

György Kara was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar who studied at Eötvös Loránd University from circa 1953 to 1958. He held a post at Indiana University from circa 1989 to 2022.
